flows.title: Home
flows.description: The returning-user dashboard. Added 2026-08-30: no Home screen existed at all, and 12 other screens' bottom-nav "Home" item pointed at discover/trending_recommended_sections as a stand-in. Information architecture is activity-first (greeting, activity counts, Continue, For you, recent activity) rather than a feature-card grid. No Firestore wiring — counts and activity are seeded sample values.

flows.title: User Auth
flows.description: Email/password calls the real Firebase Auth SDK but fails server-side (fabricated API key). OTP is 100% fake — verifyOtp()'s check is effectively "any 6-digit string passes." Google Sign-In's native flow reliably fails (fabricated OAuth client) and falls back to a fully hardcoded fake profile. Most real registrations land under a local_uid_${email.hashCode()} fallback with no corresponding Firebase Auth account.

flows.title: User Onboarding
flows.description: 13-screen real NavHost-driven flow, writes to users/{uid} on completion. instrumentProficiency, roleExperience, networkingLinks, profilePicturePath, and coverPicturePath are all collected but silently dropped from the final Firestore write.

flows.title: Add Portfolio
flows.description: 11-screen publish flow for a piece of finished creative work (song/album/EP/etc.) — distinct from the separate "Opportunities" flow's projects collection (gig/collaboration postings). Schema (portfolio_projects) corrected this session to match it exactly — ownerUid, 6 named streaming links, ownerRoles, collaborators/credits, status/visibility, artworkTheme. Zero confirmed app-side writer — PortfolioViewModel.publishProject() is still 100% in-memory with a hardcoded author name.

flows.title: Discover
flows.description: 100% mock data — DiscoverViewModel has zero Firestore references, filters a hardcoded 12-profile list. Every filterable field (experienceLevel, availabilityStatus, rating, etc.) would need to be sourced from real users/studios documents to go live.

flows.title: Opportunities
flows.description: Maps to the existing projects collection (gig/collaboration postings — someone looking for a collaborator), per the round-2 reconciliation — folded in rather than a separate gig_opportunities collection. Distinct from the "Add Portfolio" flow (finished creative work someone already made). CONFIRMED 2026-08-12 (grounded Explore audit): 100% missing, not just unconfirmed. Zero `.collection("projects")` calls anywhere in the app; `ProjectSchema` (BackendSchemas.kt:112) is defined but never instantiated. The only browse/apply UI (SuccessAndDashboardScreens.kt:2174-2435) is commented-out or unreachable dead code whose own copy admits "Opportunities are coming soon." `UnifiedOpportunityCard` is defined but never called. A "Live Opportunities Feed" nav item exists but routes to an unrelated business-storefront screen. `ChatContext.OPPORTUNITY` is just a messaging-inbox filter tab around one hardcoded demo message, not a posting/browsing flow.

flows.title: Communication & Collaboration
flows.description: connections collection has two inconsistent writers: FirebaseManager.sendConnectionRequest is correct (senderUid/targetUserId/status, composite doc ID); ConnectionsScreen.kt's second writer still writes a different, non-composite document for the same pair. chat_threads/messages exist in firestore.rules but weren't independently re-audited this session.

flows.title: Marketplace — Buy/Sell/Rent
flows.description: 100% mocked, not wired to Firestore — reconciled: MarketplaceItemDoc.category is now taxonomy-backed (marketplace_categories), matching the app's real sale/rental/mixing/beats/services split. SCREEN-MAPPED 2026-08-12 (grounded Explore audit): one real, dashboard-wired browse screen (MarketplaceBetaScreen) with 6 category tabs including "Gear Rentals", an in-dialog item detail (not a separate screen), and a Saved/Favorites bookmarks tab — all backed by hardcoded lists, zero `marketplace_items` references anywhere. No create-listing, cart, checkout, or seller-messaging screens exist at all — confirmed absent by exhaustive grep, not just unaudited. MERGED 2026-08-13 (user call): the standalone "Equipment Rental" flow entry was folded in here rather than kept separate — rental was never anything more than one of this screen's own category tabs; see the equipment_rental key's former slot (order 9, now retired, not reassigned) for the original grounded finding this merge is based on.

flows.title: Booking
flows.description: Currently studio-only (StudioBookingDoc) — not conceptually limited to studios long-term, the primary bookable entity type today is just Studio. Real writer exists but uses the wrong field names (artistUserId/totalCostAmount/statusKey instead of the schema's userId/totalAmount/bookingStatus) — confirmed still broken as of this session's last verification pass, despite two rounds of AI Studio claiming it was fixed.

flows.title: Profile Management
flows.description: profileType + Business/Band/Venue/Talent extension fields are now real schema (this session). The app previously had three disconnected profileType-guessing UI implementations (dashboard badge substring match, PublicProfilePreviewScreen headline match, Discover's mock-only enum) that should converge on the real field once wired — not independently reverified against the new field this session. IMPORTANT: this is PROFILE settings (identity, roles, links, public-facing fields) — explicitly distinct from Flow 21 "User Settings" (app preferences: notifications, privacy, dark mode, language, currency). Do not conflate the two when adding screens here.

flows.title: Services, Availability
flows.description: sessionAvailability (Talent), StudioDoc.services (taxonomy tags), and serviceOfferings (priced menu, Business) now modeled. No single unified "availability" concept spans all profile types yet — Talent/Band/Business/Venue each have their own shape.

flows.title: Business Profiles (Studios, Labels)
flows.description: UserDoc Business extension (businessName/Type/tagline/hours/GSTIN/services/equipment/teamMembers/serviceOfferings/gallery) modeled this session, matching BusinessProfileScreens.kt's mock "Octave Sound Labs" tabs. businessType only covers 4 of the PRD's ~8 sub-types (Studio/Label/School/Dealer — missing Production House/Booking Agency/Artist Manager/Rental Company).

flows.title: Notifications
flows.description: notifications/{notificationId} typed and rules-ready this session. SCREEN-MAPPED 2026-08-12 (grounded Explore audit, upgraded from "missing" to "app-mocked" — a real reader screen does exist): NotificationsCenterScreen is a genuinely reachable, feature-rich screen (search/category filters, swipe-to-dismiss, pull-to-refresh) but 100% local mock state — zero `.collection("notifications")` calls anywhere, despite UI copy that falsely claims "Firestore Real-Time Sync." Three separate, mutually-inconsistent preferences surfaces also exist (Notifications Center settings, an onboarding notification-permissions step, and a general Settings "Notification Feeds" panel) — none persist anywhere beyond local state.

flows.title: Public Profile
flows.description: Depends on Profile Management's template rendering — same profileType-driven templates. The public-facing read path wasn't separately audited this session.

flows.title: Band
flows.description: UserDoc Band extension (bandName/lineupMembers/techRiderUrl/stagePlotUrl) modeled. "Shows" (upcoming/past performances) closed 2026-08-12: `BandShow { title, date, venueName?, ticketUrl?, isPast }` + `UserDoc.shows?: BandShow[]` — a flat array, not a separate collection.

flows.title: Verifications
flows.description: verification_requests collection and the admin Verification page are both real and working. SCREEN-MAPPED 2026-08-12 (grounded Explore audit, upgraded from "missing" to "app-mocked"): one real, reachable screen (VerificationScreen) exists off the Profile tab, but it's fully simulated — upload boxes hardcode literal filenames into local state (no file picker, no FirebaseStorage call) and never write to `verification_requests`. No status-tracking (pending/approved/rejected) screen exists; verified status is three local booleans driving badge colors. `VerificationRequestSchema` is defined in BackendSchemas.kt but never instantiated.

flows.title: Reviews
flows.description: reviews collection and admin module both real and working. SCREEN-MAPPED 2026-08-12 (grounded Explore audit, upgraded from "partial" to "app-mocked" — the write side is now confirmed non-functional, not just unverified): a standalone Reputation Hub module (ReputationAndReviewsScreens.kt, reached from the dashboard, not from any post-booking prompt) has 4 real write screens — Write Review, Completed Project Review, Marketplace Gear Review, Studio Facility Review — plus business-response and report-review screens. None write to the real `reviews` Firestore collection: some persist to a local Room table, the rest are pure no-op UI. `ReviewSchema` (matching admin's ReviewDoc) exists in BackendSchemas.kt but is never referenced. The Business Profile "Reviews & Gallery" tab (already screen-mapped under business_profiles) remains a separate, read-only display of hardcoded data.

flows.title: Subscription
flows.description: Not modeled at all — no subscription/plan/tier collection exists anywhere in this schema yet.

flows.title: Search
flows.description: CORRECTED 2026-08-13 (direct source read, SupportingScreens.kt): the 2026-08-12 audit was wrong — `UniversalSearchFlow` (SupportingScreens.kt:281, reached via the dashboard's top-bar Search icon, `SupportingModule.UNIVERSAL_SEARCH`) is a real, standalone, reachable screen, not a duplicate of Discover's or Booking's internal SEARCH_RESULTS states (those remain separately covered under `discover`/`booking`). 4-state (`SearchScreenState`: HOME/LIVE/RESULTS/EMPTY), fully mocked — a hardcoded 10-item `mockAllResults` list, zero Firestore reads. `DemoDataProvider.kt`'s `searchFilterCategories` list is still confirmed dead code, unrelated to this screen.

flows.title: Recommendation Engine
flows.description: Explicitly deprioritized by the user ("ignore"). For reference: GeminiRecommendationEngine.kt is real app-side code but neutered by a placeholder-API-key guard-check bug (checks for the wrong placeholder string, so it always falls through to hardcoded fallback data).

flows.title: Settings & Support
flows.description: App-level settings (notifications/privacy/security/appearance), Help & Support (FAQ, raise a ticket, report user/listing, feedback), legal pages, and app version — explicitly distinct from Flow 1 Auth (password change lives there, not here) and Flow 10 Profile Management (identity/public-profile fields, not app preferences). user_settings/{userId} and support_tickets/moderation_flags are typed and rules-ready, but SettingsFlow and HelpAndSupportFlow app-side have zero real persistence anywhere — confirmed this session. Founded, ready-to-wire gaps, not speculative.

flows.title: CMS Pages
flows.description: page_content collection and the admin Pages module are both real and working, but frontend/website/ is 100% static HTML that never reads Firestore at runtime — edits made here don't reach the live site. Documented as a known gap (CMS_Content_Mapping.md), not silently dropped.

flows.title: QR Code & Profile Sharing
flows.description: ADDED 2026-08-13 (direct source read, previously completely absent from this registry). `QrAndShareFlow` (SupportingScreens.kt:655, reached from the dashboard's QRShare shortcut) — 3-state screen (Home/Options/Preview, plain string state, not an enum) generating a shareable "Premium Comp Card" with a simulated PDF download (fake progress bar via `delay(150)` loop, no real file generation). No schema modeled for this at all — no shareable-link record, no QR payload, no download/share analytics. `DynamicLinkManager.kt` constructs outbound share links elsewhere in the app but this screen doesn't call it — confirmed no cross-wiring.

flows.title: Saved & Favorites
flows.description: ADDED 2026-08-13 (direct source read, previously only 1 of its 4 real tabs was documented — as `marketplace_saved_bookmarks` under the `marketplace` flow, which remains accurate for that one tab). `SavedAndFavoritesFlow` (SupportingScreens.kt:1023, reached from the dashboard's Saved shortcut) is the actual hub — `SavedTab` enum: ARTISTS, BANDS, STUDIOS, MARKETPLACE (+ EMPTY state), grid/list view toggle, per-tab remove action. All four tabs are 100% local `mutableStateListOf` mock data (hardcoded artists/studios/marketplace items) — zero Firestore reads or writes, no persisted "saved" relationship on any real document.

Facility rating (acoustics/cleanliness), distinct from Business Profile's embedded Reviews & Gallery tab. Fully no-op UI, no persistence.

Dispute/report a review. Fully no-op UI, no persistence.

screens.notes: QrAndShareFlow (SupportingScreens.kt:655), reached from the dashboard's QRShare shortcut. State is a plain string, not an enum. "Preview" generates a "Premium Comp Card" with a simulated PDF download (fake progress via a delay(150) loop, no real file, no real QR payload). No schema exists for this anywhere — no shareable-link record, no download/share analytics. Does not call DynamicLinkManager.kt, despite that existing elsewhere in the app for outbound share links.

SavedAndFavoritesFlow (SupportingScreens.kt:1023), reached from the dashboard's Saved shortcut. SavedTab enum: ARTISTS, BANDS, STUDIOS, MARKETPLACE (+ EMPTY). The Marketplace tab is the same screen already documented as marketplace_saved_bookmarks under the marketplace flow (MarketplaceFeature.kt routes here, defaulted to that tab) — listed here too since it's one tab of this single real hub, not a separate implementation. All four tabs are local mutableStateListOf mock data (hardcoded artists/studios/marketplace items); zero Firestore reads or writes, no persisted "saved" relationship on any real document.

PROPOSED 2026-08-31 from the FLOW-24 brief. A collection needs its own route and deep link — it is shareable and can be opened directly — so it is a screen rather than a state of the hub. Rename/description/privacy/delete are a sheet and a dialog on this screen, not four further screens. Deleting a collection must not delete the saved items, and the copy says so.

PROPOSED 2026-08-31 from the FLOW-24 brief. A saved search is a query plus filters plus an alert toggle; running one hands off to FLOW 19 Search and alert delivery belongs to FLOW 13. This screen owns the list and the alert switch only.

PROPOSED 2026-08-31 from the FLOW-24 brief, which is explicit that Saved must never become a duplicate detail page. This shows the ORIGINAL entity preview plus the saved-specific facts (saved date, favourite state, which collection) and a single Open Original action into the canonical flow.
